Segmented control · four candidates

Bindery has five of these — Archive's grouping, Organise's view and Unify kinds, Import's state filter. Not eighteen: of the eighteen conditional buttons I lumped together, two are underline tabs that already belong to Tabs, four are sidebar nav lists, and six are single on/off toggles. Those are different problems.

This is a radiogroup, not tabs. Tabs is Radix-backed with real tabpanels and exists to switch panels. These five change what one region renders, with no panel to own — and a tablist with no tabpanel is a lie told to a screen reader. So: one choice from a set, announced as a radio group.

Click them. Everything below is real CSS on the real tokens, no JavaScript.

A · recessed track, raised thumb

The track is the page ground, cut into the surface; the selected segment rides above it on surface-raised. The thumb travels, so the change has a direction. Reads as one control.

B · bare pills, accent ground

No container. Selection is the accent tint — the loudest option, and the closest to what Bindery draws today on Archive and Import.

C · bare pills, raised ground

The same shape with the accent spent elsewhere. Quietest of the four; nearly invisible until you look for it, which is either restraint or a missing affordance.

D · one outline, hairline dividers

A single bordered unit, split by rules. The most explicit that these options are exclusive; also the heaviest, and the dividers fight the boundary at small sizes.

Equal width, or content width?

A consequence of the track, not a separate choice: a thumb that travels has to know where it is going. Equal columns make that arithmetic trivial and give the control a stable shape as the selection moves; content width is more compact and stops "Kind" from occupying as much room as "Correspondent". The real component measures the selected segment the way Tabs already measures its pill, so content width is available — but it is a different rhythm, and worth seeing side by side.

Equal columns

Stable width. "Kind" gets as much room as "Correspondent" whether it needs it or not.

Content width

Compact, and the group is narrower overall. Shown here without a travelling thumb — in the component the thumb is measured, as Tabs does.

The three things the five real sites need

Counts

Import shows a count per state. The number is part of the accessible name — "Failed, 3 items", never "Failed 3".

Icons

The vault and Photos pair an icon with each label. Decorative — the label carries the name.

Two sizes, and a disabled option

28px to sit beside a md Button, 24px for a dense toolbar. A disabled segment stays readable — it is still telling you the option exists.

What I am not asking you about. The semantics are settled by the audit, not by taste: role="radiogroup" with aria-checked, arrow keys moving the selection, one tab stop for the whole group. That is what a screen reader needs to hear for "one of these, currently the second", and it is the same contract whichever of the four you pick. The thumb travel is the --motion-tab-glide token already in the system — 280ms on the spring curve — so it matches the Tabs pill and inherits reduced-motion from the global rule.
